notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the source pages.

I tried to fetch six pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes. The first attempt failed because of a bug in my own code. The second attempt reached the pages, but the tool stopped me from running any more code for this turn before I could read what came back. The other tools I have can't reach the internet, so I couldn't try another way.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to drop anything I couldn't find. That leaves nothing to report, so I haven't written any verse-by-verse notes. I didn't fill them in from memory either, since they would have no real source behind them and the URLs could be wrong.

If you ask me again in a new message, I'll start with these pages:
- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-83/
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/83.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/83.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/83.htm
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/psalm-83-commentary (if that page exists)
- https://netbible.org/bible/Psalms+83

After that I'll search for where the traditions differ and for other views. I expect verses 9–18, the prayer against Israel's enemies, and verse 16, "that they may seek Your name," to draw the most comment. For other views I'll check the Catholic, Orthodox and modern scholarship sites, plus anything on popular readings that link this psalm to current events. I'll do fewer fetches at a time so I can read and write up each batch before the limit is reached.
